_readme: The road to the hollow's first fight, walked one tile per press - the Movement row on the
Options page turned to Tiles before the run begins. No shipped session had ever moved this way
on a real map before M51, so this is the one that says the walker survives the demo's own
walls, bodies, doors and encounters: the same held legs two_in_the_hollow.json walks, each
stopped by geometry rather than by a count, and a whole tile asserted where each one ends.
A --qa-script run empties its settings file at boot, so the choice made here is the only one.

steps.text: the title, with nothing saved, so the cursor opens on New game. Rows: Continue, New game, Credits, Options - two move_ups reach Options, one onto Continue and one that wraps round the top.
the page's rows: Sound, Window, Fights, Movement, Saving - three presses down reach Movement, and one press turns Free into Tiles
back on Options: two presses down wrap onto Continue and then New game, and the run begins
fetch Rook: south to the well, west to the wall, south to her - each leg held until a wall or a body stops it, a tile at a time
stopped by Rook's own body at [1,8], so the player stands on the tile north of her, on its centre
north up the wall and through the west door, which a step meets by landing on it. The hold carries past the warp, so the next leg re-anchors against the hollow's own geometry.
south until the wall, then west along the only row that reaches the gap the slink is standing in - and the fight opens on the tile the last step LANDS on, beside it
and the player is still on the tile the fight began on: a fight does not move anybody
